walkthroughs.body_html:
Magnetism & Electromagnetism — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Magnetism & Electromagnetism brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Magnetism & Electromagnetism.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 2 kg object accelerates at 4 m/s². What is the resultant force?
options: 2 N
8 N
6 N

mcqs.q: What does it mean if the resultant force on an object is zero?
options: The object must be stationary.
The object is either stationary or moving at constant velocity.
The object is decelerating.
The object is accelerating.

mcqs.q: In a balanced nuclear equation, what must be equal on both sides?
options: Only the total mass in kilograms needs to balance.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
Only the atomic number (proton count) needs to balance.
The total mass number (top numbers) and the total atomic number (bottom numbers) must both balance.

mcqs.q: Why do transformers only work with alternating current?
options: DC cannot enter a transformer because the iron core blocks it.
A transformer needs a changing magnetic flux in the core; DC produces a steady flux and so no emf is induced in the secondary.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
Transformers work with DC too, just less efficiently.

mcqs.q: After one half-life, what happens to an individual radioactive nucleus?
options: The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
Only the total mass in kilograms needs to balance.
Every nucleus is guaranteed to have half-decayed after one half-life.
It has a 50 percent chance of having decayed — radioactive decay is random for any single nucleus.
